As vibe coding (programming through AI prompts) becomes increasingly popular, the number of new apps submitted to the App Store has surged, doubling in the first half of 2026—though downloads have only grown by 2%. Here's the full summary.

The number of new app submissions has risen sharply, but downloads lag far behind

The New York Times published a report today, citing the latest data from Sensor Tower, noting that while new App Store submissions doubled in the first half of 2026, downloads rose by only 2%.

The report also focused on two developers who have been continuously releasing vibe coding apps on the App Store: Marco Pérez plans to quit his job at JPMorgan next month to work on app development full-time; David Svensson, on the other hand, has launched 11 niche apps over the past five months, treating vibe coding as a hobby rather than a business.

Excerpts from the report are as follows:

Pérez is a software engineer based in Chicago who had never developed a mobile app before. He spent five weeks during the winter researching "vibe coding" AI tools to build a prototype, then took an additional two weeks to prepare for App Store submission. His app, InfoDrizzle, performed reasonably well, accumulating 1,300 downloads and earning around US$500 in profit. Pérez's next app proved even more popular. In May, he spent roughly one week launching Stampa, a scrapbooking app that transforms photos into digital stamps. Stampa has since been downloaded 20,000 times, generating around US$3,000 in profit.

Apple spokesperson Peter Ajemian, in response to the New York Times, mentioned another issue arising from the surge in submissions: earlier reports indicated that the App Store review process has come under pressure as a result.

Ajemian stated: "Apple has consistently been able to review 90% of app submissions within 48 hours", and added that Apple "welcomes a new generation of developers using the latest tools to build and launch apps at unprecedented speed".

He also pointed out that all apps "must meet the same high standards of quality, privacy and security that users have always trusted, regardless of whether they are developed using vibe coding".
